stories.title: Amazon doesn’t trust Meta’s Muse AI agent
stories.sum: Meta's Muse AI agent has been blocked from shopping Amazon on behalf of its users, GeekWire reports.

stories.title: Santiago Sierra’s latest piece, a non-stop reading of names of Palestinians killed since 1948, opens in London
stories.sum: Organised by A/POLITICAL, the continuous reading by Arabic speakers will be open to the public, as well as available to view via livestream

stories.title: The Book of Alison Knowles
stories.sum: A retrospective traces the language of bookmaking in her expansive work and its radical influence on American art.

stories.title: Christie’s Wins Battle for Herbert Lust Collection, Expected to Fetch More Than $50 M.
stories.sum: A $20 million–$30 million Alberto Giacometti sculpture leads the group, which heads to sale in November.

stories.title: The Big Review: Lucas Museum of Narrative Art ★★★½
stories.sum: While the swooping building is impressive and easy to navigate, the collection is patchy and the displays are at times “bizarre”

stories.title: Carolina Caycedo’s Raw Materials
stories.sum: The artist and activist rages against environmental destruction and the efforts to call those responsible to account
also: The New York Times — Art & Design

stories.title: Amar Kanwar review: unflinching Indian artist dares you to step into the darkness (literally)
stories.sum: Serpentine North, London Making lyrical films for over 40 years, about everything from the end of empire to sexual brutality, Kanwar focuses on the parts of gruesome stories that are often missed The exhibition begins…

stories.title: Louis Vuitton Unveils Keith Haring Artycapucines Handbag Collection
stories.sum: The brand plans to present some of the designs at Art Basel Paris alongside Artycapucines bags from previous editions.

stories.title: Inside the Self-Enclosed Universe of Henri Alexander Levy
stories.sum: The founder of the cult fashion label Enfants Riches Déprimés speaks about discipline, self-destruction, and why provocation, for him, was never the point. Louis Lu
